description: Curated candidate relationships. Analytical hypotheses are explicitly labelled and should not be treated as proven causal effects.

assumptions: Global supply tightness persists and is transmitted into relevant market prices.
caveats: IEA global market assessment; not a direct forecast of UK pump prices.

assumptions: Road transport businesses use diesel and pass some additional fuel costs into operating costs.
caveats: The size of the effect depends on fuel contracts, hedging, margins and efficiency.

assumptions: Some businesses pass a portion of increased transport costs to customers.
caveats: Not all businesses pass costs on; other cost and demand factors matter.

assumptions: Household owns or uses a diesel vehicle or is otherwise exposed to fuel-related travel costs.
caveats: The record concerns global diesel markets, not an individual household's pump price.

edges.relationship: sets regulated default-tariff price limits for
evidence_status: Household is on a tariff covered by the cap.
assumptions: The cap limits unit rates and standing charges; it is not a fixed annual bill.

edges.pathway: Retail energy rates → household energy expenditure
assumptions: Consumption, region, payment method and tariff are considered.
caveats: Actual bills vary with consumption and tariff.

edges.pathway: ONS CPI release → consumer price inflation
evidence_status: The ONS release is interpreted using its stated CPI definition.
assumptions: An aggregate CPI rate is not an individual household inflation rate.

edges.pathway: Household Cost Indices → purchasing power pressure
assumptions: Household group expenditure patterns are relevant to the comparison.
caveats: Group averages are not individual household budgets; HCI is not a personal forecast.

edges.relationship: can erode when income growth lags
assumptions: Nominal household income or benefits do not rise as quickly as relevant prices.
caveats: The impact varies with household-specific spending and income changes.

edges.pathway: Bank Rate → mortgage and credit payments
assumptions: A household has variable-rate borrowing or refinances at a higher rate.
caveats: Fixed-rate borrowers are affected mainly at product renewal; lender pricing differs.

evidence_status: The OBR's conditioning assumptions are interpreted as forecast context.
assumptions: This is not a Bank of England commitment or a guaranteed future rate.

edges.pathway: Higher rent → household disposable income after housing costs
edges.time_lag: at rent review or tenancy change
assumptions: Rent increases apply to the household and income does not rise enough to offset them.
caveats: Actual exposure depends on tenancy, rent review timing, income and housing support.

edges.pathway: Rent burden → ability to save for a deposit
assumptions: A prospective buyer rents and has limited surplus income.
caveats: Not all renters are prospective buyers; savings behaviour and income vary.
